name: Jobber
tagline: Quoting, scheduling, invoicing and payments software for home service businesses like landscaping, HVAC and cleaning.

pricing.basis: monthly, tiered by plan and number of users
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of Jobber is boring CRUD: clients, properties, quotes, jobs on a calendar, invoices, and a running balance. An agent can absolutely build that in a weekend, and for a one-truck operator a local app with a client list and a PDF invoice generator covers most of the daily grind. The parts that hurt are the ones you cannot fake in a sitting: taking card payments, texting customers automated reminders, a crew-facing mobile app that works with one bar of signal, and clean two-way sync with your accounting. Jobber also sits on top of money movement and tax paperwork, which is where DIY stops being fun. Build it if you are solo and already invoice by email; do not build it if you have four techs and a bookkeeper.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you keep clients and properties, turn a quote into a scheduled job, and turn a completed job into a numbered invoice you can print or email as PDF.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to keep it running if you want calendar access from the field
Stripe account and API key if you want payment links
Twilio or similar if you want SMS reminders, otherwise reminders are just emails
whatYouLose: Card and ACH payments handled for you, including saved cards, deposits and tips
A real mobile app for crews with offline job details, time tracking and photo uploads
Automated customer texts: on-my-way messages, reminders, review requests
QuickBooks sync, so your bookkeeper gets a spreadsheet instead
Recurring job scheduling, route optimization and multi-tech dispatch that actually holds up when someone calls out
moatNotes: Moving money and reconciling it with accounting software is the part that keeps customers, not the calendar.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is not the product, the cash flow is. Jobber gets a quote accepted on a phone in a driveway, charges the card, pushes the invoice into QuickBooks and nags the customer for a review, all without the owner opening a laptop at 9pm. A self-hosted job tracker gives you the records but leaves you doing the collection, the reminders and the bookkeeping by hand, and every hour of that is billable work you did not do. Add three employees who need a phone app and the math stops being close.
notes: Perfectly reasonable weekend build for a one-person operation, and a bad idea the moment payroll exists.
prompt:
Build a local-first field service job tracker for a one-person home service business. Single user, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/app.db
- Server actions for all writes, no separate API layer
- Runs with: npm install, npx prisma migrate dev, npm run dev

Data model:
- Client: name, phone, email, notes
- Property: belongs to a Client, address, access notes
- Quote: belongs to a Property, line items (description, qty, unit price), status draft/sent/approved/declined, total computed
- Job: optional link to an approved Quote, scheduled start and end datetime, assigned note, status scheduled/in-progress/complete, visit notes
- Invoice: generated from a Job, invoice number auto-incrementing, line items copied from the quote and editable, status draft/sent/paid, amount paid, balance

Screens:
- Dashboard: today's jobs, unsent invoices, unpaid balance total
- Week calendar view of Jobs, click a day to add a job, drag not required
- Clients list with search, client detail showing properties, quotes, jobs, invoices
- Quote editor with line items and a Convert to Job button
- Job detail with Mark Complete which offers Create Invoice
- Invoice detail with a print stylesheet so Cmd-P produces a clean one-page PDF

In scope: seed script with three fake clients and a week of jobs, currency formatting, basic validation, mobile-friendly layout for the job list and job detail.

Out of scope, do not build: payment processing, SMS, email sending, multi-user roles, recurring jobs, route optimization, accounting sync, file uploads.

If you add a Stripe payment link field on Invoice, read the key from .env only and leave it optional. Write a README with the three commands to run it and one paragraph on backing up data/app.db.
